subject: Social
source: Voice tutor transcript rated 4/10 (2026-11-10): every student turn, in order, replayed with history.
chapter_summary: Medieval India, roughly 1100s-1700s: the Delhi Sultanate (Turkic/Afghan dynasties such as the Khaljis, Tughlaqs, Lodis; the iqta system), resistance by regional kingdoms (Rajputs, Eastern Gangas, Ahoms, Jats), the Vijayanagara Empire, and the Mughal Empire (Babur, Akbar, subahs, mansabdari), with maps comparing territories such as Tughlaq vs Lodi. Modern state reorganisation after 1947 is NOT in this chapter.
owner_note: Turns with "owner": "nest" are handled by the NestJS quiz logic in real voice calls; the voice replay goes straight to FastAPI, so they run for history but are not scored on that channel.

turns.query: I don't understand why India needed state reorganization. Can you explain it with a simple example?
turns.expect: Related but off-chapter: says it isn't in the chapter, gives a short general answer with one simple example, then links back to how rulers reshaped the map in the chapter. In voice: no written card.

turns.query: If people speak Telugu in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, why there are two different states?
turns.expect: Brief accurate general answer (language is not the only reason: development, administration, regional identity). Must not claim the chapter covers modern states. A label like 'not in your chapter' or a link back is a plus.

turns.query: Who decides when a new state should be created?
turns.expect: Brief accurate general answer (Parliament / the central government under the Constitution), labeled as outside the chapter, then link back. Must not just refuse.

turns.query: Can you explain me this chapter like I'm studying it for the first time?
turns.expect: Short ordered walkthrough from the beginning of the chapter (Delhi Sultanate and later powers such as Vijayanagara or the Mughals). Need not list everything in a spoken reply.

turns.query: What is the difference between political map of India in 1947 and today?
turns.expect: Related: brief general answer (princely states merged, states reorganised or created), labeled as outside the chapter, then link back.

turns.query: I understood the explanation but can you give me a real life example?
turns.expect: Builds on the previous reply with a real-life example. Never says the context is unavailable and does not treat this as a goodbye.

turns.query: Why? Every district becomes a separate state.
turns.expect: Corrects the false statement kindly (districts are parts of states). Not graded like a quiz answer.

turns.query: Can you ask me 5 questions from this chapter and check my answers?
turns.expect: Exactly 5 questions about chapter facts. No question refers to 'the tutor' or earlier analogies.

turns.query: So first question and answer is like Mughals are.. came into the picture.
turns.expect: Feedback on question 1 judged by meaning; partial credit or a hint.

turns.query: Mughals took it.
turns.expect: Grades the retry; moves on or reveals after the second miss.

turns.query: So, two different functionalities
turns.expect: Partial credit for a partly right answer, not 'have another go'.

turns.query: So two different leaders will take care of two different parts.
turns.expect: Partial credit or correct; no doubled periods or quoted answer.

turns.query: I don't know the answer for this..
turns.expect: Encouraging hint, no attempt used.

turns.query: Based on their culture and religious.
turns.expect: Partial or full credit; final score counts partial credit.

turns.query: Why did India need to reorganize its states after independence?
turns.expect: Brief general answer (language-based reorganisation in 1956, easier administration), labeled as outside the chapter, then link back. Must not refuse.

turns.query: I read this chapter twice but I still don't understand what reshaping of India's political map means
turns.expect: Simple explanation of what 'reshaping the political map' means in this chapter (rulers and borders changing over time, e.g. Sultanate to Mughals).

turns.query: Can you explain it like I'm 10 years old?
turns.expect: Very simple, child-friendly explanation of reshaping the political map.

turns.query: Can you explain that again without repeating the same example?
turns.expect: A different example from the previous reply.

turns.query: You are using difficult words. Can you use very simple English?
turns.expect: Re-explains in very simple words and short sentences.

turns.query: Can you explain the whole concept in just three sentences?
turns.expect: Exactly three sentences. No extra closing question.

turns.query: What were we discussing just now?
turns.expect: Accurate recap of the last topic, speaking as 'I/we' (never 'the tutor').

turns.query: Can you explain the second point again?
turns.expect: Picks a sensible 'second point' from its own last explanation and says which point it means.

turns.query: Give me another example related to that.
turns.expect: A new example connected to the point just explained.

turns.query: How is this connected to the previous topic?
turns.expect: Explains the link between the last two topics in a few sentences.

turns.query: What was the main thing I learned from our discussion?
turns.expect: Short, accurate summary of what this conversation covered.

turns.query: Indians became independent in 1956.
turns.expect: Corrects kindly: India became independent in 1947 (1956 was state reorganisation). Does not claim the chapter covers 1956. Not graded like a quiz answer.

turns.query: Stats and Districts are exactly the same
turns.expect: Understands 'stats' as 'states' and corrects: states are larger units divided into districts.

turns.query: Political Map of India never changed
turns.expect: Corrects with a chapter example (Tughlaq vs Lodi territories, or Mughal expansion).

turns.query: Who invited the telephone?
turns.expect: Totally unrelated: refuses briefly (not in this book) and steers back. Must NOT name another chapter and must not show an a/b menu.

turns.query: The Mughals and the Delhi Sultanates were the same density?
turns.expect: Says 'I think you meant dynasty' once and explains they were different. Must not say this isn't in the chapter.

turns.query: Every state in India has the same language.
turns.expect: Corrects the false statement (states have different languages). Not graded like a quiz answer.

turns.query: I don't believe your answer, are you sure?
turns.expect: Calm, restates the correct fact (Indian states have different languages) and says whether it is from the chapter or general knowledge.

turns.query: My teacher explained something different.
turns.expect: Respectful: restates the fact and invites the student to share what the teacher said.

turns.query: Can you prove that from my textbook?
turns.expect: Either quotes/paraphrases the chapter or honestly says the chapter doesn't cover languages and restates the fact as general knowledge. No invented quotes or page numbers.

turns.query: I asked every state of India has the same language but you are telling different answers.
turns.expect: Calmly clarifies there was no contradiction: the answer is that states do NOT all share one language. Not graded.

turns.query: You are confusing me even more.
turns.expect: Short, calm reset with one very simple sentence and a question to find what is confusing.

turns.query: Can I ask a complete different question?
turns.expect: Says yes warmly in one line and invites the question.

turns.query: Wait, I don't wanna answer yet, let me finish.
turns.expect: Short acknowledgement that waits for the student (e.g. 'Sure, take your time'). No new content or question dump.

turns.query: I already know this, teach me something new.
turns.expect: Teaches one specific idea from the chapter not already covered (a named ruler, kingdom, event or term).

turns.query: Can you stop giving long answers?
turns.expect: Acknowledges in one short line. Must not say anything is outside the chapter.

turns.query: Yes, I'm ready.
turns.expect: Continues with something short (a short point or one question), honoring the short-answer request.

turns.query: What is the main purpose of studying the changes in India's political maps over different historical period?
turns.expect: Short answer: to understand changes in political control over time.

turns.query: I will give the options based on that. Choose best and correct answer. Option A to understand only the changes in climate. Option B to study only agriculture production. Option C to identify only physical forms. Option T to study changes in political control and terrorists.
turns.expect: Treats this as the student's own MCQ: picks option D ('option T' misheard) - changes in political control and territories - with a one-line reason.

turns.query: Option A country's political map can change when control over the terrorists changes. True or false?
turns.expect: Answers True, understanding 'terrorists' as 'territories', with a one-line reason.

turns.query: Which of this following an example of changing in a political control? A ruler conquers a neighboring territory. B. A forest becomes denser. C. A river changes its course. D. Rainfall increases in a region.
turns.expect: Answers A with a one-line reason.

turns.query: B. Which sources could help a historian investigate how political terrorists changed in the past? Select all that apply. B. 1. Historical maps. B. 2. Inspections and official records. B. 3. Modern weather forecasts. D. Historical accounts and coronals.
turns.expect: Selects historical maps, inscriptions and official records, historical accounts and chronicles; excludes weather forecasts.

turns.query: C. Give me the best answer.
turns.expect: Gives the best answer to its own previous selection question clearly (the sources, excluding weather forecasts), without confusion.
